verses.1:1: Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that is in accord with godliness,
verses.1:2: in hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before eternal ages,
verses.1:3: and at the proper times manifested His word through the proclamation with which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior,
verses.1:4: to Titus, a genuine child in a shared faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
verses.1:5: For this reason I left you behind in Crete, so that you would set in order the things remaining and appoint elders in every city, just as I directed you:
verses.1:6: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not under an accusation of debauchery or insubordinate.
verses.1:7: For the overseer must be blameless as God's steward: not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain,
verses.1:8: but hospitable, a lover of what is good, prudent, righteous, devout, self-controlled,
verses.1:9: holding firmly to the trustworthy word according to the instruction, so that he may be able both to exhort in sound teaching and to reprove those who contradict.
verses.1:10: For there are many who are insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
verses.1:11: who must be silenced, since they are overturning entire households by teaching things they ought not for the sake of shameful gain.
verses.1:12: One of them, a prophet of their own, said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."
verses.1:13: This testimony is true. For this reason reprove them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith,
verses.1:14: not paying attention to Jewish myths and the commands of people who turn away from the truth.
verses.1:15: All things are pure to the pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; instead, both their mind and their conscience have been defiled.
verses.1:16: They profess to know God, but by their deeds they deny Him, being detestable and disobedient and disqualified for every good work.
verses.2:1: But as for you, speak the things that are fitting for sound teaching.
verses.2:2: Older men are to be temperate, dignified, prudent, sound in faith, in love, in endurance.
verses.2:3: Older women likewise are to be reverent in demeanor, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good,
verses.2:4: so that they may train the young women to love their husbands and to love their children,
verses.2:5: to be prudent, pure, workers at home, good, submitting to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be maligned.
verses.2:6: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be prudent;
verses.2:7: in all things showing yourself to be a pattern of good deeds, in teaching displaying integrity, dignity,
verses.2:8: and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
verses.2:9: Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not talking back,
verses.2:10: not pilfering, but showing all good faithfulness, so that they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior in everything.
verses.2:11: For God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
verses.2:12: training us so that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live prudently, righteously, and godly in the present age,
verses.2:13: awaiting the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
verses.2:14: who gave Himself on our behalf so that He might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for Himself a people of His own possession, zealous for good deeds.
verses.2:15: Speak these things, and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one disregard you.
verses.3:1: Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
verses.3:2: to malign no one, to be peaceable and considerate, showing all gentleness toward all people.
verses.3:3: For we ourselves were also once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, spending our lives in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.
verses.3:4: But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
verses.3:5: not by works in righteousness that we ourselves did, but according to His mercy He saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
verses.3:6: whom He poured out abundantly on us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
verses.3:7: so that, having been justified by His grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
verses.3:8: The word is trustworthy, and concerning these things I want you to insist confidently, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are good and profitable for people.
verses.3:9: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, strifes, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and futile.
verses.3:10: Reject a factious person after a first and second warning,
verses.3:11: knowing that such a person is warped and is sinning, being self-condemned.
verses.3:12: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
verses.3:13: Diligently help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that nothing may be lacking for them.
verses.3:14: And let our own people also learn to devote themselves to good deeds for pressing needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
verses.3:15: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith. Grace be with all of you.

notes.1:1: Greek kata ('according to') may here denote either standard ('in accordance with') or goal ('for the faith of God's chosen ones').
notes.1:6: Greek tekna ... pista ('faithful children') is debated and can also be translated 'believing children.'
notes.1:12: The saying is attributed in antiquity to the Cretan poet Epimenides (6th century BC); 'lazy gluttons' is literally 'idle bellies.'
notes.2:5: Greek oikourgous ('workers at home') is the reading of the earliest manuscripts, whereas later manuscripts read oikourous ('keepers at home').
notes.2:11: The phrase 'to all people' may modify either the adjective 'bringing salvation' or the verb 'has appeared' ('has appeared to all people, bringing salvation').
notes.2:13: Because a single Greek article governs both 'great God' and 'Savior,' most grammarians understand both titles as referring to Jesus Christ; some alternatively read 'of the great God and of our Savior Jesus Christ.'
notes.3:5: The phrasing may be construed either as two parallel means ('through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit') or with both genitives dependent on 'washing.'
notes.3:8: The Greek idiom kalon ergon proistasthai ('devote themselves to good deeds'; also in 3:14) can refer both to practicing good deeds and, in some contexts, to engaging in honorable occupations.
notes.3:10: Greek hairetikon ('factious' or 'divisive') denotes one who causes divisions or factions rather than the later technical sense of 'heretical.'
